routes.label: Reflect B and use similar triangles

question: Let \(\triangle ABC\) be a scalene triangle. Point \(P\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(\overline{AP}\) bisects \(\angle BAC.\) The line through \(B\) perpendicular to \(\overline{AP}\) intersects the line through \(A\) parallel to \(\overline{BC}\) at point \(D.\) Suppose \(BP = 2\) and \(PC = 3.\) What is \(AD?\)
solution:
Add \(Q\), where \(BD\) meets \(AC\). This creates an isosceles triangle around the angle bisector and a pair of similar triangles using the parallel lines.

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_10A_Q13_official_solution_fig1.png)

Let \(M=AP\cap BQ\). The right triangles \(AMB\) and \(AMQ\) share \(AM\) and have equal angles at \(A\), because \(AP\) bisects \(\angle BAC\). They are congruent, so \(AB=AQ\).

The angle bisector theorem in \(ABC\) now gives
\[
\frac{AC}{AQ}=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{PC}{PB}=\frac32.
\]
Since \(AC=AQ+QC\), it follows that \(QC/AQ=1/2\).

Triangles \(CQB\) and \(AQD\) are similar: they have equal vertical angles at \(Q\), and \(BC\parallel AD\). Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{BC}{AD}=\frac{QC}{QA}=\frac12.
\]
But \(BC=2+3=5\), so \(AD=\boxed{10}\), choice C.

The added intersection joins two useful clues: an angle bisector gives side ratios, and parallel lines turn those ratios into the requested length.
